name: Fairmont Sonoma Mission Inn & Spa
positioning: Spanish Mission-style spa resort in Sonoma, California, built around geothermal mineral springs (official name Fairmont Sonoma Mission Inn & Spa)
best_for: Travelers who want a spa stay centred on geothermal pools
Families and pet owners who want a wine country base

facts.text: The resort is at 100 Boyes Blvd in Sonoma, California.
The current Spanish Mission-style retreat was built after a previous hotel burned down in a wildfire in 1923.
A water tower stands above the resort's tiled roof.
The grounds have gurgling fountains and 100-year-old redwood and eucalyptus trees.
Santé Restaurant and 38º North Wine Bar are on the property.
Fairmont rooms in the historic Mission building have Provence-inspired decor.
The resort offers complimentary cruiser bikes, a kids' lounge and daily wine tasting.
The family-friendly Resort Pool is filled with naturally heated geothermal water and is open year-round.
Hotel guests have access to the Sonoma Golf Club during their stay.
The hotel is pet-friendly and charges a per-pet fee per stay.

highlights.text: Fairmont Spa sits atop an ancient mineral hot spring that feeds five geothermal pools.
The area has been known since Indigenous peoples first discovered healing mineral hot springs there.
The Gloria Ferrer Suite has decor inspired by Sonoma's sparkling wine producer.
The Jack London suite has decor inspired by the American novelist who called Sonoma his hometown.

considerations.text: Parking is outdoors and costs extra.
Sonoma County Airport is the closest airport, in Santa Rosa, so the resort is reached by road from there.
WhataHotel notes this is a popular destination that requires advance booking.
